Forecast one or more series

Source: R/forecaster.R
timestral_forecast.Rd

Zero-shot probabilistic forecast with 21 quantiles per step.

Usage

timestral_forecast(
  model,
  y,
  h,
  observation_mask = NULL,
  past_covariates = NULL,
  known_covariates = NULL,
  categorical_past_covariates = NULL,
  categorical_known_covariates = NULL,
  symmetric = TRUE,
  clip_nonnegative = TRUE
)

Arguments

model

a timestral_model

y

numeric vector, ts/mts, zoo/xts (index preserved), a tsibble (keys become the batch, measured variables the jointly forecast variates), matrix or data frame with time in rows and one column per target variate, a 3-D array (time, variate, series), or a list of per-series vectors/matrices (NA = missing). The series of a list (or the key groups of a tsibble) may differ in length: they are taken to end at the same time, the forecast origin, and shorter ones are left-padded with missing values, which does not change their forecasts. A list keeps the longest series' time index when every other series' index is its tail (for ts, the same frequency and end). Variates of a series are forecast jointly; series in a batch are forecast independently in one call. Covariates may also be ts/zoo/xts or tsibble; when both y and a covariate carry a time index, the covariate index must align with the context (and future) index of y. Tsibble rows are taken in index order, and implicit gaps in a regular tsibble are filled with missing values; the keys of a keyed tsibble covariate are matched to the series of y by value.

h

horizon in steps: a single whole number between 1 and 10000

observation_mask

optional logical shaped like y (for a tsibble y, a tsibble with logical measured variables); FALSE or NA marks additional missing values

past_covariates

known over the context only (T time rows, or the batch forms described for y; in a batch of unequal lengths, a shorter series' covariates may have its own length, and are padded like it)

known_covariates

known over context and horizon (T + h time rows)

categorical_past_covariates

category codes known over the context only; target-encoded per series (used as-is when a series has several target variates)

categorical_known_covariates

category codes over context and horizon

symmetric

average with the forecast of the mirrored series (package default)

clip_nonnegative

clip at 0 when every observed target value is >= 0

Value

a timestral_forecast: for one series, quantiles is a (variate, horizon, level) array; for a batch, (series, variate, horizon, level). Also holds the observed context values (with NA for missing), and the context index and future_index when y carried a time index (ts, zoo, xts); the future index extends the last observed interval.

Examples

## the tiny bundled checkpoint runs offline but its forecasts are
## meaningless; use timestral_load("5M") or larger for real ones
m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
## univariate ts: index preserved, fan chart and ts accessors work
fc <- timestral_forecast(m, AirPassengers, h = 24)
plot(fc)

timestral_median(fc)
#>           Jan      Feb      Mar      Apr      May      Jun      Jul      Aug
#> 1961 291.3287 360.7115 280.6464 318.2002 223.7060 189.5016 350.5766 244.7158
#> 1962 260.1235 270.1221 257.1679 300.3938 292.1597 363.0654 276.1783 315.2443
#>           Sep      Oct      Nov      Dec
#> 1961 270.5898 313.5198 281.9475 301.3957
#> 1962 227.9375 200.5240 348.4063 245.5896

## multivariate: columns of y are forecast jointly
fc2 <- timestral_forecast(m, cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths), h = 12)

## zoo/xts inputs keep their time index (needs the zoo package)
if (requireNamespace("zoo", quietly = TRUE)) {
  months <- seq(as.Date("1949-01-01"), by = "month",
                length.out = length(AirPassengers))
  yz <- zoo::zoo(as.numeric(AirPassengers), order.by = months)
  fc3 <- timestral_forecast(m, yz, h = 24)
  head(as_forecast_df(fc3))   # time column holds Dates
}

if (requireNamespace("tsibble", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fc4 <- timestral_forecast(m, tsibble::as_tsibble(AirPassengers), h = 24)
  tsibble::as_tsibble(fc4)
}
